questions.question: P alone can complete a piece of work in 10 days while Q alone can complete the same piece of work in 15 days. To complete the work in 4 days, R is hired by P and Q. How many days does R take to complete the work alone?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(10, 15, 4) = 60 units

Efficiency: P = 6, Q = 4, P + Q + R = 15

Efficiency of R = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units/day

Time for R alone = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P = 10 days

Time taken by Q = 15 days

Time taken by P + Q + R together = 4 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Entity
 Time
 Quantity
 Efficiency
 
 

 P

 60

 4
 
 

 P + Q + R

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of P + Q + R = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of R = (Efficiency of P + Q + R) − (Efficiency of P + Efficiency of Q)

⇒ Efficiency of R = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by R alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of R

⇒ Time taken by R alone = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency of the worker. Time = 1 ÷ Efficiency (keeping work constant).

Combined Work Formula

If A, B, and C can do a work in x, y, and z days respectively, their combined 1-day work is (1/x + 1/y + 1/z).

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct ratio of the amount of work done, which is also the ratio of efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: Of the 5 subjects, the average marks of Rakesh in first 3 subjects was 75 and the average marks in the last 3 subjects was 82. If his marks in the third subject was 66, then what was his average marks in all the 5 subjects?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average mark of Rakesh in the first 3 subjects was 75

The average marks in the last 3 subjects were 82

Rakesh's marks in the third subject were 66

**Formula:**

Average = Total marks/Number of subjects

**Calculation:**

Find the total marks Rakesh scored in the first 3 subjects

Average = Total marks/Number of subjects 

Total marks in first three subject = 75 × 3 = 225

Find the total marks Rakesh scored in the last 3 subjects

Total marks in the last 3 subjects = 82 × 3 = 246

Find the total marks Rakesh scored in all 5 subjects

Total marks in all 5 subjects = Total marks in the first 3 subjects + Total marks in the last 3 subjects - Marks in the third subject

225 + 246 - 66

225 + 246 - 66

405

Find the average marks of Rakesh in all 5 subjects

Average marks in all 5 subjects = Total marks in all 5 subjects/Number of subjects

= 405/5

= 81

**So, Rakesh's average mark in all 5 subjects was 81.**

questions.question: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 126. What is the product of the smallest and the largest numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 126.

**Formula:**

The sum of n consecutive even numbers can be found using the formula: n/2 × (first number + last number)

Calculation:

The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 126, which can be represented as x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 126, where x is the smallest of the three numbers.

To find the value of x, we can simplify the equation and solve for x:

3x + 6 = 126

3x = 120

x = 40

**Therefore, the smallest of the three numbers is 40, the largest is 40 + 4 = 44, and the product of the smallest and the largest numbers is 40 × 44 = 1760.**

questions.question: Sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm. What is the radius of the circumcircle of this triangle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm, and 9 cm

Formula used:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle]

Calculation:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Side of the triangle are, a = 12 cm, b = 9 cm and c = 9 cm, then

s = (12 + 9 + 9)/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm

Area of the triangle = √[15 (15 – 12) (15 – 9) (15 – 9)] = √[15 × 3 × 6 × 6] = √5 × 6 × 3 = 18√5 cm2

As we know,

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle] = (12 × 9 × 9)/(4 × 18√5) = (27√5)/10

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The weight of Ayush and Abhishek are in the ratio of 8 ∶ 5. Abhishek's weight increases by 40 percent and the total weight of Ayush and Abhishek both increase by 60 percent. If the total weight becomes 104 kg, then what is the weight of Ayush after the increment?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The new total weight is 104 kg, which represents a 60% increase (or 160% of the initial weight).

Initial total weight = 104 ÷ 1.6 = 65 kg.

Initial weight of Abhishek = (5 / 13) × 65 = 25 kg.

New weight of Abhishek (after 40% increase) = 25 × 1.4 = 35 kg.

New weight of Ayush = Final total weight − New weight of Abhishek = 104 − 35 = 69 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 69 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial weight ratio of Ayush to Abhishek = 8 : 5

Abhishek's weight increases by 40%.

Total weight increases by 60% to become 104 kg.

 Initial Total Weight = 65 kg (100%)
 
 
 Ayush: 40 kg
 Abhishek: 25 kg
 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 +40%
 
 
• 
 

 +60% overall

 Final Total Weight = 104 kg (160%)
 
 
 Ayush: 69 kg
 Abhishek: 35 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial weight of Ayush be 8x and Abhishek be 5x.

⇒ Total initial weight = 8x + 5x = 13x

⇒ The total weight increased by 60%, making the final weight 160% of the initial.

⇒ 13x × (160 / 100) = 104

⇒ 13x × 1.6 = 104

⇒ 20.8x = 104

⇒ x = 104 ÷ 20.8 = 5

⇒ Initial weight of Abhishek = 5x = 5 × 5 = 25 kg

⇒ New weight of Abhishek = 25 × (140 / 100) = 35 kg

⇒ Final weight of Ayush = Final total weight − Final weight of Abhishek

⇒ Final weight of Ayush = 104 − 35 = 69 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 69 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

When a value increases by R%, the new value becomes Base Value × (1 + R/100). Here, a 60% overall increase means multiplying the base weight by 1.6 to get the final total weight.

Weighted Average (Alligation Method)

The overall percentage change is the weighted average of the individual percentage changes: Overall % = (Ratio₁ × Change₁ + Ratio₂ × Change₂) ÷ Total Ratio.

Ratio Independence

When quantities are given in a fixed ratio, their actual individual values can be directly scaled and calculated as soon as the total initial or final amount is known, skipping the need for multiple variables.
</p

questions.question: In a mixture, milk and water are in ratio of 1 ∶ 4. Some milk is added to the mixture because of which ratio of milk and water becomes 2 ∶ 1. How much milk was added as a percentage of initial mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since only milk is added, the quantity of water remains constant throughout.

Initial Milk : Water = 1 : 4

Final Milk : Water = 2 : 1 ⇒ 8 : 4 (Multiplying by 4 to equalize the water parts)

Milk added = Final milk parts − Initial milk parts = 8 − 1 = 7 units.

Total initial mixture = 1 + 4 = 5 units.

Percentage of milk added = (7 ÷ 5) × 100 = 140%.

**∴ The correct answer is 140%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of Milk to Water = 1 : 4

Final ratio of Milk to Water = 2 : 1

 
 Initial Mixture
 M : W = 1 : 4
 Total = 5 units

 
 Final Mixture
 M : W = 8 : 4
 Total = 12 units

 
• 
 
 
 

 
 
 + Milk added
 (Water constant)
 
 
 Milk added = 8 − 1 = 7 units
 % Added = 7 ÷ 5 × 100 = 140%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial amount of milk be x and water be 4x.

⇒ Total initial mixture = x + 4x = 5x

⇒ Let y amount of milk be added to the mixture.

⇒ New amount of milk = x + y

⇒ The amount of water remains the same, which is 4x.

⇒ The new ratio of milk to water becomes 2 : 1.

⇒ (x + y) ÷ 4x = 2 ÷ 1

⇒ x + y = 8x

⇒ y = 7x

⇒ Milk added as a percentage of initial mixture = (Amount of milk added ÷ Total initial mixture) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (7x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = 1.4 × 100 = 140%

**∴ The correct answer is 140%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Component Principle

When only one component (like milk) is added or removed from a mixture, the quantity of the other component (like water) remains constant. Equating the ratio parts of the constant component provides the fastest way to solve mixture problems.

Rule of Alligation

A foundational concept used to quickly evaluate the ratio in which two mixtures or distinct ingredients must be combined to yield a required average concentration.

Relative Percentage Calculation

To express an added quantity as a percentage of the original quantity, always use the formula: % Added = (Added Value ÷ Initial Base Value) × 100.
</p

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 20 percent more than its cost price. What maximum discount percentage can be offered by the shopkeeper to sell his article so that there is no loss?
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price of an article is 20% more than its cost price.

Formula:

Marked price = Cost price + (20% of Cost price)

Discount = Marked price - Selling price

To avoid any loss, the selling price should be equal to or greater than the cost price.

Solution:

Let's assume:

The cost price of the article = 100

Marked price = 100 + (20/100) × 100

Marked price = 120

To avoid any loss, the selling price should be equal to or greater than the cost price:

Selling price ≥ Cost price

Now let's calculate the maximum discount percentage that can be offered by the shopkeeper:

Discount = Marked price - Selling price

Discount = 120 - 100

Discount = 20

To avoid any loss, the selling price should be equal to or greater than the cost price:

Selling price ≥ Cost price

Discount = 20

Maximum discount percentage = (Discount/Marked price) × 100

Maximum discount percentage = (20/120) × 100

Maximum discount percentage = (1/6) × 100

Maximum discount percentage = 16.67%

Therefore, the maximum discount percentage that can be offered by the shopkeeper to sell the article without any loss is 16.67%.

questions.question: What is the value of an angle subtended by a chord at the centre of the circle, if the angle subtended by this chord at the circumference is 66° ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **angle subtended** by an arc at the **centre** of a circle is **double** the angle subtended by it at the **circumference**.

∠Centre = 2 × ∠Circumference

∠Centre = 2 × 66° = 132°

**∴ The correct answer is 132°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle subtended by the **chord** at the **circumference** = 66°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7feef29b50fda3068774d2bf57587c4ead2676df288e59a761c2e8cc6da5bf30.png] 

According to the **Circle Theorem**, for a **chord** AB:

⇒ Angle at Centre (∠AOB) = 2 × Angle at Circumference (∠ACB)

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 66°

⇒ ∠AOB = 132°

**∴ The correct answer is 132°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same **arc** or **chord** at any points on the remaining part of the **circumference** are always **equal**.

Angle in a Semi-circle

The angle subtended by the **diameter** at any point on the **circumference** is always a **right angle** (90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the **opposite angles** of a **cyclic quadrilateral** (a quadrilateral where all vertices lie on a circle) is 180°.</p

questions.question: If sin θ = √3 cos θ, then what is the value of (3sin ² theta +cos theta)/(2cos theta +5)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: **sin θ = √3 cos θ** ⇒ **tan θ = √3**.

For tan θ = √3, the value of **θ = 60°**.

Substitute θ = 60° in the expression: (3 sin² 60° + cos 60°) ÷ (2 cos 60° + 5).

⇒ [3 × (3/4) + 1/2] ÷ [2 × (1/2) + 5] = (9/4 + 2/4) ÷ (1 + 5) = (11/4) ÷ 6 = 11/24.

**∴ The correct answer is 11/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sin θ = √3 cos θ ⇒ sin θ / cos θ = √3 ⇒ tan θ = √3 / 1

**Formula Used:** tan θ = p/b | h = √(p² + b²) | sin θ = p/h | cos θ = b/h

⇒ p = √3, b = 1 ∴ h = √((√3)² + 1²) = √(3 + 1) = 2

⇒ sin θ = √3 / 2 and cos θ = 1 / 2

⇒ Value = [3 × (√3/2)² + (1/2)] ÷ [2 × (1/2) + 5]

⇒ Value = [3 × (3/4) + 1/2] ÷ [1 + 5]

⇒ Value = [9/4 + 2/4] ÷ 6 = (11/4) ÷ 6 = 11/24

**∴ The correct answer is 11/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Specific Angles

Standard values: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

Right Angled Triangle Properties

questions.question: Radius of a circle is 18 cm. Angle made by chord AB at the centre of this circle is 60 degree. What is the length of this chord?
questions.solution:
Given:

The radius of a circle is 18 cm. The angle made by chord AB at the center of this circle is 60 degrees.

Concept used:

1. In an Isosceles triangle, the two angles opposite to the equal sides are equal to each other.

2. In an equilateral triangle, since the three sides are equal therefore the three angles, opposite to the equal sides, are equal in measure.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40b850cf96d2c8eb3de332637e72dda5d7c8cc6bded78385112090aadcde558e.png] 

OA = OB = 18 cm

ΔOAB is an isosceles triangle.

So, ∠OAB = ∠OBA = frac {(180 - 60)^circ}{2} = 60° 

Since ∠OAB = ∠OBA = ∠OAB = 60°, ΔOAB is an equilateral triangle.

So, OA = OB = AB = 18 cm

∴ The length of this chord is 18 cm.

questions.question:
Vivek starts moving at the speed of 70 km/hr at 8 ∶ 00 am. Neeraj starts moving in the same direction after 4 hours of Vivek at the speed of 120 km/hr. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Neeraj and Vivek meet each other at 5 ∶ 36 pm.

II. Total distance covered by both Neeraj and Vivek till 4 pm is 1080 km.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let's first calculate the distance Vivek covers from 8:00 am to 12:00 pm (4 hours):

Distance covered by Vivek = Speed × Time
